ARCH=HEX,DI,DIP,NO_CROSS_LAYER,PORT_FLOW_OUT_IN,SEVERITY
APP.NAME=newspipe
APP.LANGUAGE=Python
APP.VERSION=0.2.0-SNAPSHOT
LAYER.ORDER=domain,application,infrastructure,control
ARCH.HEX=Hexagonal. DOMAIN holds value types, APPLICATION owns the port and the use cases, INFRASTRUCTURE implements the port, CONTROL parses arguments, constructs the adapter and prints. The launcher is one file, so the four layers are four sections in that order from the top of scripts/newspipe.py to the bottom.
ARCH.DI=CONTROL constructs SubprocessOps once and passes it to every use case. No service locator and no module-level mutable singleton.
ARCH.DIP=OpsPort is an abstract base class declared in the APPLICATION section. SubprocessOps in the INFRASTRUCTURE section implements it. The use cases name OpsPort only and never name SubprocessOps.
ARCH.NO_CROSS_LAYER=Section dependencies point one way. DOMAIN imports nothing from the other three sections, APPLICATION imports DOMAIN, INFRASTRUCTURE imports DOMAIN and APPLICATION, CONTROL imports all three above it.
ARCH.PORT_FLOW_OUT_IN=Outbound port OpsPort declared in APPLICATION, adapter SubprocessOps in INFRASTRUCTURE implementing it.
ARCH.SEVERITY=Every CU in this ITR is implicitly SEVERITY:CRITICAL. A stub, a missing verb, a missing annotation or a mypy error is a hard fail. Report and stop.
ARCH.PYTHON.EXPLICIT_DECLARATION=MUST, CRITICAL. Every variable carries an annotation at first binding, either name: Type = value or name: Type before assignment. Every function parameter and return type is annotated too.
ARCH.PYTHON.NO_ANY=MUST, CRITICAL. typing.Any never appears and no generic is left bare. dict, list, tuple and set always state their parameters, for example tuple[str, ...].
ARCH.PYTHON.SLOTTED_FROZEN_DATACLASS=SHOULD, MAJOR by default. Data classes use @dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True) unless the class genuinely needs mutation. This ITR declares no exception.
ARCH.PYTHON.MONADIC_ERROR=SHOULD, MAJOR by default. Expected failures travel as Ok or Err. try/except exists only to convert an OSError or a subprocess failure into Err, never to swallow it.
ARCH.TYPE_PROBE=uvx mypy --strict scripts/newspipe.py must exit 0 with zero errors. No standalone mypy binary exists on this host, uvx is the runner.
ARCH.NO_PIPELINE_EDIT=HARD_FAIL. Nothing under pipelines/** is created, modified or deleted by any CU here. The logback file reaches the forked application JVM through JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, never through build.sbt.
ARCH.NO_INFRA_EDIT=HARD_FAIL. Nothing in ~/Repos/pipeline_infra is edited. terraform appears only as a command executed by the up verb.
ARCH.NO_DESTROY=HARD_FAIL. terraform destroy appears in no step, no acceptance command and no CU. Every volume and the shared network carry prevent_destroy, so a destroy cannot succeed on this host.
ARCH.LAUNCHER_STATE=/tmp/newspipe-launcher.state is launcher bookkeeping, not a log. One tab-separated line per recorded child: pid, pipeline name, newest poll line observed. No history and no rotation. It is the only file the launcher writes.
ARCH.LOGGING_EXTERNAL=conf/logback.xml at the repository root is the only logging configuration in this repository. Neither pipeline tree gains src/main/resources/logback.xml.
ARCH.STDOUT_ONLY=stdout only. No log shipping, aggregation, rotation or log file on disk anywhere in this ITR.
ARCH.OUT_OF_SCOPE=Infra teardown, Trino, Hive Metastore, silver and gold layers and any edit to ~/Repos/pipeline_infra are addressed by no CU in this ITR.

LEGEND.PROVE_LINE=A `Prove: ` backtick-quoted shell command that proves the preceding step succeeded. Every numbered step carries one.
LEGEND.DO_NOT_TOUCH=A closed list of paths the Coder must not modify. Violation is a MAJOR architecture deviation.
LEGEND.STOP_WHEN=The condition under which the Coder halts and reports rather than continuing.
LEGEND.OK_ERR=Ok and Err are the two monad data classes. A value you want is Ok(value), a failure you expect is Err(exception). Callers branch on isinstance(result, Err) instead of catching.
LEGEND.MAYBE=A type written T | None is present-or-absent without an exception. None means the reading could not be taken, never that the value is zero.
LEGEND.LITERAL=Literal[...] is a closed vocabulary of exact strings. PipelineName accepts exactly "ingestion" and "enrichment" and nothing else type-checks.
LEGEND.ABC_PORT=An abstract base class whose @abstractmethod bodies raise NotImplementedError. It is the contract, SubprocessOps is the implementation.
LEGEND.STATE_LINE=One tab-separated line in /tmp/newspipe-launcher.state: pid, pipeline name, newest observed poll line. Exactly three fields; any other shape is ignored.
LEGEND.JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=An environment variable the JVM reads at startup and converts into -D system properties. Both pipelines set run / fork := true, so this is the only channel that reaches the forked application JVM without editing build.sbt. Its single cost is one "Picked up" line on stderr, which carries no HEARTBEAT and no poll line.
LEGEND.READINESS=The three dependencies up waits for: Kafka on TCP 9092, RustFS answering 200 on /health, and opencode present on PATH. All three names come from ReadinessGate in the ingestion tree.
LEGEND.CU_ID=Zero-padded three-digit identifier, cu-001 through cu-003.
LEGEND.WAVE=An ordered group of CUs that may run in parallel because they touch disjoint files.
LEGEND.CRITERION_REF=A numbered acceptance criterion from the feat-9 specification.

REQUIREMENTS:
Deliver feat-9 criterion 1: a single external logging configuration at the repository root.

The enrichment entry point logs one informative line per cycle, logger.info("poll merged " + n + " enriched units") in pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala, but no logback*.xml exists anywhere in either pipeline tree while logback-classic is on both dependency lists. Logback therefore falls back to BasicConfigurator, the root logger runs at DEBUG, and the Kafka coordinator heartbeat writes a DEBUG line every three seconds underneath the two lines that carry information.

This CU writes conf/logback.xml beside the existing conf/feeds.conf, conf/ingestion.conf and conf/enrichment.conf, so logging levels become external user configuration in the same place as the other external settings. The newspipe logger is set to INFO so every newspipe.* record survives, the three noisy library families and the root logger are set to WARN so the heartbeat disappears, and the console appender keeps the existing line shape.

The file is XML, not code, and it is the whole deliverable. The launcher is a separate CU and nothing else in this repository changes.

COORDINATES:
FILE.conf/logback.xml
FILE.conf/feeds.conf
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala

# IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:

1. Create `conf/logback.xml` at the repository root, beside `conf/feeds.conf`, with exactly this content.

```xml
<configuration>
  <appender name="STDOUT" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
    <encoder>
      <pattern>%date{HH:mm:ss.SSS} %-5level [%thread] %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
    </encoder>
  </appender>

  <logger name="newspipe" level="INFO"/>
  <logger name="org.apache.kafka" level="WARN"/>
  <logger name="org.apache.spark" level="WARN"/>
  <logger name="org.apache.hadoop" level="WARN"/>
  <logger name="org.sparkproject" level="WARN"/>
  <logger name="io.delta" level="WARN"/>

  <root level="WARN">
    <appender-ref ref="STDOUT"/>
  </root>
</configuration>
```

Prove: `test -f conf/logback.xml && grep -c '<root level="WARN">' conf/logback.xml`

2. Confirm `conf/logback.xml` is the only logging configuration in the repository and that neither pipeline tree gained one.

```sh
test -f conf/logback.xml
find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*' | wc -l
```

Prove: `test -f conf/logback.xml && find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*' | wc -l`

3. Confirm the informative line's logger is covered by the `newspipe` logger level in `conf/logback.xml`, so criterion 2 can hold once a pipeline is started.

```sh
grep -n 'logger.info("poll merged' pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala
grep -n 'name="newspipe" level="INFO"' conf/logback.xml
```

Prove: `grep -c 'name="newspipe" level="INFO"' conf/logback.xml`

Do NOT touch: `pipelines/**`, `conf/feeds.conf`, `conf/ingestion.conf`, `conf/enrichment.conf`, `scripts/`, `~/Repos/pipeline_infra/**`, `.LLMDD/**`

Stop when `conf/logback.xml` cannot be written at the repository root, or when step 2 prints a non-zero count, meaning a second logging configuration exists somewhere under `pipelines/`. Report which of the two happened rather than continuing.

ACCEPTANCE:
AC-1 (criterion 1) `test -f conf/logback.xml` exits 0.
AC-2 (criterion 1) `find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*'` prints nothing, so conf/logback.xml is the only logging configuration.
AC-3 The newspipe logger carries level INFO and the root logger carries level WARN: `grep -c 'name="newspipe" level="INFO"' conf/logback.xml` prints 1 and `grep -c '<root level="WARN">' conf/logback.xml` prints 1.
AC-4 No file under `pipelines/**` changed: `git status --porcelain pipelines/` prints nothing.

REQUIREMENTS:
Prove feat-9 end to end: criteria 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 against the live stack, after the logging configuration and the launcher both exist.

This CU creates, modifies and deletes no repository file. It runs the launcher as a user would and records what the probes print. Every child started here is stopped by the launcher's own down verb before this CU ends, and the one destructive-looking action in the whole feature, stopping the rustfs container for the negative readiness probe, is restored immediately in the same step.

The end-to-end run is what no unit test can cover. Criterion 2 and criterion 3 are claims about a live Kafka consumer's stdout, and criterion 5, criterion 6 and criterion 7 are claims about process lifecycle across two separate launcher invocations. They are asserted here rather than in the creation CU so that the launcher's own creation CU can run in parallel with the logging CU, since neither of those two depends on the other.

The negative readiness probe carries a risk worth stating plainly: terraform apply runs before the readiness check, and if the docker provider restarted a stopped container during apply the probe would heal itself. pipeline_infra declares rustfs as a docker_container resource with no start or must_run attribute, so an apply with a stopped container reports no configuration change and leaves it stopped, and the readiness check then fails as intended. If apply does restart it on this host, criterion 8's negative case cannot be proven and that fact is reported rather than worked around.

COORDINATES:
FILE.scripts/newspipe.py
FILE.conf/logback.xml
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala
FILE.pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala

# IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:

1. Confirm `conf/logback.xml` exists and is the only logging configuration before any pipeline is started.

```sh
test -f conf/logback.xml
find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*' | wc -l
```

Prove: `test -f conf/logback.xml && find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*' | wc -l`

2. Shorten the next enrichment cycle so the `scripts/newspipe.py run enrichment` start in step 3 completes inside a wait, by shifting `enrichment-group` to three messages behind the topic end.

```sh
docker exec kafka /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --group enrichment-group --topic raw_rss --reset-offsets --shift-by -3 --execute
```

Prove: `docker exec kafka /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --describe --group enrichment-group`

3. Start `scripts/newspipe.py run enrichment` in the background with its stdout captured to a scratch file, then wait for the poll line to appear in that file.

```sh
python3 scripts/newspipe.py run enrichment > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log 2>&1 &
for i in $(seq 1 60); do grep -q 'poll merged [0-9]* enriched units' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log && break; sleep 5; done
```

Prove: `grep -c 'poll merged [0-9]* enriched units' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log`

4. Assert the two log-legibility criteria on the captured stdout of `scripts/newspipe.py run enrichment`: zero heartbeat lines and at least one informative poll line.

```sh
grep -c HEARTBEAT /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log || echo "zero HEARTBEAT lines"
grep -E 'poll merged [0-9]+ enriched units' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log
```

Prove: `grep -c HEARTBEAT /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log; grep -c 'poll merged [0-9]* enriched units' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log`

5. Run `scripts/newspipe.py status` from a second invocation while the enrichment child is still running, and confirm all four readings including the newest poll line.

```sh
python3 scripts/newspipe.py status > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-status.log 2>&1
cat /tmp/newspipe-feat9-status.log
```

Prove: `grep -cE 'raw_rss: [0-9]+ message|enrichment-group: committed=[0-9]+|poll merged' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-status.log`

6. Stop the children with `scripts/newspipe.py down` and confirm they are gone while Kafka and RustFS stay up and no terraform process appeared.

```sh
python3 scripts/newspipe.py down
test ! -f /tmp/newspipe-launcher.state && echo "no children recorded"
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E '^(kafka|rustfs)$' | sort
pgrep -af terraform | wc -l
```

Prove: `python3 scripts/newspipe.py down; test ! -f /tmp/newspipe-launcher.state && echo cleared`

7. Assert criterion 5 by starting each selection through `scripts/newspipe.py run` in turn and counting the reported children as one, one and two, stopping between each.

```sh
python3 scripts/newspipe.py run ingestion > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-ingestion.log 2>&1 &
sleep 30
grep -c '^started pid=' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-ingestion.log
python3 scripts/newspipe.py down
python3 scripts/newspipe.py run enrichment > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment2.log 2>&1 &
sleep 30
grep -c '^started pid=' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment2.log
python3 scripts/newspipe.py down
python3 scripts/newspipe.py run both > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-both.log 2>&1 &
sleep 30
grep -c '^started pid=' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-both.log
python3 scripts/newspipe.py down
```

Prove: `grep -c '^started pid=' /tmp/newspipe-feat9-both.log`

8. Assert criterion 8's negative case on `scripts/newspipe.py up`: stop rustfs, expect a non-zero exit naming rustfs, then start rustfs again in the same step.

```sh
docker stop rustfs
python3 scripts/newspipe.py up > /tmp/newspipe-feat9-up-fail.log 2>&1; echo "up exit=$?"
grep -i rustfs /tmp/newspipe-feat9-up-fail.log
docker start rustfs
```

Prove: `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -c '^rustfs$'`

9. Assert criterion 8's positive case on `scripts/newspipe.py up` once all three dependencies are reachable again.

```sh
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E '^(kafka|rustfs)$' | sort
python3 scripts/newspipe.py up
```

Prove: `python3 scripts/newspipe.py up | tail -1`

10. Assert criterion 11 after the full run: no file under `pipelines/**` was created, modified or deleted by any of the preceding steps.

```sh
git status --porcelain pipelines/
```

Prove: `git status --porcelain pipelines/ | wc -l`

Do NOT touch: any file in this repository. This CU runs probes only. In particular `scripts/newspipe.py` and `conf/logback.xml` are read-only here, `pipelines/**` is read-only, and `~/Repos/pipeline_infra/**` is another repository that no CU in this ITR may modify. The only state the launcher writes outside the repository is /tmp/newspipe-launcher.state and the scratch capture files under /tmp.

Stop when any probe disagrees with its acceptance line. Report the failing criterion number, the exact command and its output, and stop rather than editing `scripts/newspipe.py` or `conf/logback.xml` to make a probe pass. A repair belongs to a new CU issued by the Designer.

ACCEPTANCE:
AC-1 (criterion 1) After the run, `test -f conf/logback.xml` exits 0 and `find pipelines -name 'logback*.xml' -not -path '*/target/*'` prints nothing.
AC-2 (criterion 2) `grep -c HEARTBEAT /tmp/newspipe-feat9-enrichment.log` prints 0, and the same capture contains a `newspipe` record at INFO, so the heartbeat flood is gone while informative records survive.
AC-3 (criterion 3) The same capture contains at least one line matching `poll merged [0-9]+ enriched units`, visible without grep on the live output.
AC-4 (criterion 5) The child counts printed for run ingestion, run enrichment and run both are 1, 1 and 2 respectively, and no verb started a pipeline it was not asked for.
AC-5 (criterion 6) After down, /tmp/newspipe-launcher.state is absent, no launcher-recorded child survives, and `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'` still lists kafka and rustfs.
AC-6 (criterion 7) `python3 scripts/newspipe.py down` exits 0 while `pgrep -af terraform` shows no process started by it.
AC-7 (criterion 8, negative) With rustfs stopped, `python3 scripts/newspipe.py up` exits non-zero and names rustfs in its output.
AC-8 (criterion 8, positive) With kafka, rustfs and opencode all reachable, `python3 scripts/newspipe.py up` exits 0 and its last line matches `ready: kafka, rustfs, opencode`.
AC-9 (criterion 9) /tmp/newspipe-feat9-status.log contains a `raw_rss` count line, an `enrichment-group` committed and lag line, and a line containing `poll merged`.
AC-10 (criterion 11) `git status --porcelain pipelines/` prints nothing after the full run.
